visual_brief.subject: A multi-agent reliability claim widens when the fallible voter becomes part of the system
verified_context: The preprint models individual agents, workload uncertainty and the combining mechanism as one failure network that produces a reliability envelope.
In one chemical-hazard extraction case, majority voting protected against the weakest model but did not clearly outperform the best model.
The result is preliminary, narrow and not independently reproduced.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: Redundancy cannot create a defensible reliability claim when the component that combines the agents is left outside the evaluation.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: Three dark stone arches focus through a suspended glass voter whose fissures widen the terracotta uncertainty field beneath it.

candidate_notes.A: Constitution-compliant. The monumental gate and layered paths fit the archive, but the three agent inputs are less immediately legible.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant. The three weighted signals and loosened voter joint communicate the mechanism strongly, though the horizontal convergence reads slightly diagram-first.
candidate_notes.C: Selected. Three arches and a visibly fissured suspended lens make the voter part of the physical system while the broad terracotta field communicates uncertainty without invented data.

crop_review.article_desktop: The three arches, cracked lens and terracotta uncertainty field remain visible across the wide crop.
crop_review.article_mobile: A centered cover crop retains the suspended voter and the central portions of all three input arches.
crop_review.thumbnail: The cracked translucent lens over the terracotta field remains the dominant silhouette at 320px.

golden_reference_comparison: The selected candidate shares the research references' pale monumental geometry, sparse terracotta signal, suspended scientific-object quality and confident negative space. Its translucent material is more photographic than the references' line-led treatment, so fit is scored at 87.
